svg.aria-label: Diagram: what a Microsoft Entra B2B guest user is and how guest access is governed. A B2B collaboration user object is created in the same directory as employees, with a UserPrincipalName of the form user_contoso.com#EXT#@tenant.onmicrosoft.com. UserType is either Member or Guest and has no relation to how the user signs in or their directory role, and UserType and the Identities property are independent, which produces four categories: external guest, external member, internal guest and internal member. Before redemption the account has no credentials, the Identities property is the host organization domain, externalUserState returns Pending Acceptance, and the inviting user is recorded in the Sponsor attribute. After redemption Identities becomes ExternalAzureAD, Microsoft Account, google.com, facebook.com, mail for email one-time passcode, or an issuer URI for a SAML or WS-Fed provider. Email one-time passcode is on by default for new tenants, and phone sign-in is not supported for external users. The three guest access levels are Same as member users with role template value a0b1b346-4d3e-4e8b-98f8-753987be4970, Limited access as the default with value 10dae51f-b6af-4016-8d66-8c2a99b929b3 where guests can see membership of all non-hidden groups, and Restricted access with value 2af84b1e-32c8-42b7-82bc-daa82404023b where guests can view only their own profile and group name and email columns appear blank with group type Unrecognized. Changes take up to 15 minutes to take effect. Regardless of level, guests cannot enumerate the list of groups or users. The four guest invite settings range from anyone in the organization including guests, which is the default, through member users and specific admin roles, through only specific admin roles, to no one including admins; the Guest Inviter role can still invite even when only admin roles are permitted. Restricted permissions are unsupported in Forms, Project Online, Viva Engage and Planner in SharePoint, and do not override SharePoint or Teams guest settings. Sign-in logs are written in both the home tenant and the resource tenant.
svg.title: A guest is a row in your own directory carrying a label, and the label is not the boundary
svg.text: A guest is a user object “in the same directory as your employees”, carrying one attribute.
“The UserType has no relation to how the user signs in, the directory role of the user, and so on.” It is a label for policy, not a boundary.
The two defaults that decide your external population
Who can invite a guest
“all users… including B2B collaboration guest users” — guests invite guests
What a guest can read
“Guests can see membership of all non-hidden groups”
But read the FAQ before over-correcting: “Regardless of default or restricted guest permissions, guests can’t enumerate the
list of groups or users.” The real leak is narrower — a guest pivots from their own object ID to their own memberships, and
on the default level sees “all the group details, including name, email”. Group names are where orgs document themselves.
Three levels, one property on authorizationPolicy
LEVEL
WHAT THE GUEST SEES
guestUserRoleId
Same as members
everything a member can
Limited (default)
their groups, with name and email
Restricted
own profile only; name and email blank,
Group Type shows “Unrecognized”
Changes “can take up to 15 minutes to take effect”. No new licence. Existing tenants were not changed — so nobody will do it for you.
Four invite levels, and a documented bypass
1. Anyone, including guests and non-admins — THE DEFAULT
2. Member users plus specific admin roles
3. Only users assigned to specific admin roles
4. No one in the organization, including admins
Guest Inviter invites even on level 3 — by design, so that
delegation does not need a higher admin role.
So that role’s membership IS part of the invite policy.
The object, before and after redemption
UPN: user_contoso.com#EXT#@tenant.onmicrosoft.com
Before: no credentials at all; externalUserState returns
“Pending Acceptance”
And the inviter is recorded automatically in the Sponsor
attribute — the answer to “who let this person in”.
After: Identities becomes ExternalAzureAD, Microsoft
Account, google.com, facebook.com, mail (email OTP), or a
SAML / WS-Fed issuer URI. Phone sign-in is not supported.
Two independent attributes make four categories — and one escapes every guest filter
“Identities and UserType are independent properties.” So: external guest · external member · internal guest · internal member.
An EXTERNAL MEMBER authenticates in a tenant you do not control and is typed Member. Governance keyed on
UserType eq ‘Guest’ cannot see them at all — not in filters, not in reports, not in access reviews.
Restricting is not free, and the directory setting does not win
Supported with Restricted
Teams · Outlook · SharePoint · Planner in Teams · Project for the web
Not supported
Forms · Project Online · Viva Engage · Planner in SharePoint
How that failure presents
in Viva Engage, guests “aren’t able to leave the group” — a dead button
Does it override SharePoint / Teams?
“No. Those existing settings still control the experience and access”
Effective guest access is the intersection of four independently-owned things: the Entra permission level, the invite policy,
SharePoint and Teams sharing, and cross-tenant access settings. One reassurance: sign-in logs are written in BOTH tenants.
Sources: B2B guest user properties, Restrict guest user access permissions, and Configure external collaboration, on Microsoft Learn.
